In summary, our research is concerned with
how accounting is used as a means of organizing.
the role of accounting in the organization of the economy.
how accounting and accountability practices shape the organization of work and, in turn, are shaped by the organization of work.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

accounting is the language of business and it is used by the managers and other stakeholders of an organisation to measure, record, summarise, analyse and interpret the financial information of the organisation.
the accounting information system is the backbone of any business organization and it is the most important tool that helps the business organization to function smoothly.

accounting is the art of recording, classifying, and summarizing in a significant manner and in terms of money, transactions and events which are, in part, at least of a financial character, and interpreting the results thereof.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
accounting is a social practice that is constitutive of organizing.
accounting and finance are the two most important disciplines for the study of the economic aspects of business.
accounting and organizing are mutually constitutive and are both constitutive of economizing.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is a need to develop a more sophisticated understanding of the role of accounting in organizing, and that the accounting-organizing-economizing nexus can be a useful lens through which to do so.
accounting is not only a way to measure performance, but also a way to shape it.
accounting and finance are not separate disciplines, but are in fact deeply interconnected.
